sources.title: Constructing geologically-constrained 3D models using 3D GeoModeller: an example from the Paterson Orogen
Graphical Expression for Logical Model of Geologic Structure by Binary Tree

claimSourcePairs.locator: PDF printed page 2, section 3, stratigraphic-pile bullet
claimSourcePairs.reason: The source establishes a stratigraphic pile and contact relations, but does not directly define deposition as adding younger material with non-negative thickness.

claimSourcePairs.locator: Article abstract, sentence describing a sequence of sedimentation and erosion
claimSourcePairs.reason: The abstract supports sedimentation as a formative event in a recursive logical model, but not the implementation-specific non-negative-thickness statement.

claimSourcePairs.locator: PDF printed page 3, Paterson Formation discussion
claimSourcePairs.reason: The source describes a younger formation onlapping an erosional surface that dissects older sedimentary and basement units.

claimSourcePairs.locator: Article abstract, recursive definition of structures formed by sedimentation and erosion
claimSourcePairs.reason: The abstract supports erosion as a formative event but does not directly state the project's geometric truncation rule.

claimSourcePairs.locator: Full PDF keyword and contextual review
claimSourcePairs.reason: No direct definition of depositional thickness converging to zero was identified.
The accessible primary abstract discusses sedimentation and erosion, not pinch-out geometry.

claimSourcePairs.locator: PDF printed pages 2-3, stratigraphic-pile bullet and Paterson Formation discussion
claimSourcePairs.reason: The source explicitly uses onlap as a contact relation and gives a younger unit on an older erosional surface as an example.
Onlap is not stated in the accessible primary abstract.

claimSourcePairs.locator: PDF printed page 3, zero-thickness non-depositional erosion-surface discussion
claimSourcePairs.reason: The text concerns representation of an erosion surface and does not support elapsed time without geometric removal.
The accessible primary abstract does not define nondeposition.
